entries.note: Neither everybody being wrong nor a nightmare to untangle has a shared evidentiary threshold.
He explicitly says GPUs may meet this fate.
The allegation concerns deliberate deception, rather than simply whether the capacity figures are accurate.
Calling the situation a huge scandal is a judgment of worth.
The advance-sales assertion is explicitly qualified by may and potentially.

entries.test: Public financial statements and project disclosures showing the aggregate construction in progress of the listed excluded operators and projects at publication.
entries.note: I think introduces a numerical estimate rather than an explicit probability.

entries.test: The stated CIP inputs and allocation arithmetic, together with inventory disclosures, would establish whether the assumptions support approximately $234 billion of warehoused GPUs and TPUs.
entries.note: The assumptions concern a present estimate, not a future event.

entries.test: Public shipment, installation and inventory records showing the installed share of Hopper GPUs and the number of uninstalled Blackwell GPUs at publication.
entries.note: The wording endorses an estimate with identifiable quantities.
Materially changes everything specifies no common test for the claimed consequence.
Functionally useless evaluates the estimates' usefulness without specifying an accuracy criterion.

entries.test: Microsoft's and other operators' public capacity announcements would show whether they systematically conflate overall or secured power capacity with operational AI capacity.
entries.note: The surrounding examples give the colloquial accusation a concrete reading.

entries.test: OpenAI's original end-2025 disclosure and public capacity allocations would establish what its 1.9GW figure specified and implied about Microsoft and Oracle infrastructure.
entries.note: He asserts that OpenAI made an ambiguous claim; he does not independently assert ownership of 1.9GW.
A spending problem is an evaluative characterization.

entries.test: Future hyperscaler financial statements would show whether GPU depreciation spikes or the assets instead enter a disclosed write-off program.
entries.note: The plain accounting reading is a depreciation spike unless the GPUs are written off; no deadline is given.
The composite assertion expressly attributes implicit knowledge to every purchaser. Purchase volumes and installation delays alone cannot establish that private knowledge.

entries.test: Public capex, installed-asset and inventory records would establish whether his stated assumptions support $791 billion unaccounted for and approximately $395 billion in uninstalled silicon.
entries.note: Questionably legal accounting refers to hypothetical paper-only sales, not to storing purchased silicon.

entries.test: Contemporaneous investor and press coverage, compared with commissioning records and capex totals, would show whether revenue growth was credited to investments that remained largely undeployed.
entries.note: The quoted praise is reported, but the criticism and deployment assertion are Zitron's own.

entries.test: Public customer revenue breakdowns, compute allocations and growth disclosures would show whether OpenAI and Anthropic account for the asserted revenue shares and growth across the named providers.
entries.note: I believe does not by itself turn this causal assertion into a possibility claim.

entries.test: Public groundbreaking, construction and operational commissioning dates for AI data centers would establish whether typical completion takes years.
entries.note: It appears frames an evidence-based observation about construction duration.

entries.test: Public project completion records, press reports and audience research would show whether coverage systematically overstates completion and causes outsiders to overestimate buildout progress.
entries.note: Willingly or otherwise makes deliberate intent unnecessary to the claim.

entries.test: Public 2026 debt issuance records and financing documents would establish the $290 billion total, construction uses and prevalence of repayment tied to customer project revenues.
entries.note: The substantive claim concerns existing debt structures; may or may not exist describes customer uncertainty.
The central assertion ranks stopping sales or financing as the best outcome.
The installation forecast explicitly says likely. The proposition also omits the commitment that prices fall even without significant available capacity.

entries.test: Applicable securities law, disclosure rules and judicial or regulatory interpretations would establish whether NVIDIA has the stated disclosure obligation.
entries.note: He asserts an existing legal responsibility, not merely a preferred policy.

entries.test: Public customer concentration, advance-purchase, inventory and production-capacity records would show whether hyperscalers exceed half of NVIDIA revenue and their stockpiling alone constrains supply.
entries.note: The attribution of supply constraints is a substantive causal claim.

entries.test: Public purchaser deployment and revenue disclosures, together with shipment and inventory records, would show whether most purchased GPUs remain warehoused and most buyers have generated little revenue from them.
entries.note: The proposition faithfully extracts the factual assertions without the separate disclosure recommendation.

entries.test: Public chip sales concentration, downstream utilization and revenue data, and Huang's statements would show whether the demand cycle is driven entirely by those large buyers and unsupported revenue claims.
entries.note: Entirely is a strong causal commitment that contrary demand evidence could challenge.

entries.test: Public debt totals, consumer electronics price series, market earnings exposure and GPU customer utilization data would test the asserted borrowing, inflation, dependence and nonuse.
entries.note: The sweeping language does not remove its factual commitments.

entries.test: Public GPU purchase and deployment records, cloud customer revenue concentration and the labs' financial results would show whether NVIDIA's growth mainly funds prospective capacity dependent on OpenAI and Anthropic spending.
entries.note: Speculative purchasing has a concrete contextual meaning: purchases ahead of deployment and realized revenue.

entries.test: Public shipment and deployment valuations, hyperscaler disclosures and investment-flow evidence would test the $200 billion undeployed estimate and the claimed contribution of disclosure practices to speculative investment.
entries.note: Absorbed by the market means operational deployment in this context.
Maybe explicitly qualifies the $22 billion figure.

entries.test: Future operational capacity, utilization, compute demand and distressed-asset outcomes would establish whether the current buildout produces sustained excess capacity and investment losses.
entries.note: Inevitable makes the overbuild forecast firm despite its undated horizon.
The central claim judges Anthropic's influence as a historic misallocation. Its embedded 5GW feasibility allegation is separately testable.

entries.test: Public operational capacity and procurement records would show whether 5GW was available to Anthropic at publication and whether an additional 10GW becomes available during 2027.
entries.note: The present-capacity component is already assessable; the 2027 component is not due.
He presents this universal failure as a feared possibility rather than a firm finding.

entries.test: Public neocloud financial results, defaults, restructurings and customer contract disclosures would show whether their debt dependence leads to severe financial distress.
entries.note: Financial ruin makes the highway-to-Hell metaphor more specific than the source warrants. The surrounding debt claim still gives the warning a testable financial reading.

entries.test: Public lifetime deployment and customer revenue records for the GPUs sold by publication, together with financing protections, would show whether at least 90% never generate revenue and investors lack recourse if demand fails.
entries.note: I don't see how expresses a firm negative expectation here. Revenue refers to purchasers' use of GPUs, not NVIDIA's sale proceeds.

entries.test: Future financial statements, debt recovery records and big-tech public statements would establish tens of billions in write-downs, total investor losses on failed deals and admissions that capex was wasted.
entries.note: The double negative conveys an expectation, not merely a possibility.
He expressly counts embarrassment, poor earnings and destruction alike as losing. That range supplies no shared test for whether every investor ultimately loses.

entries.test: Following any bailouts, public AI compute revenues, infrastructure investment returns and hyperscaler growth would establish whether sufficient demand materializes to sustain the capex and long-term growth.
entries.note: Not that I think we will refers to stopping the buildout, not to whether bailouts will happen. The forecast expressly applies even under a bailout scenario.
